title: Greeting Decision Path
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Trace an if/elif/else chain that picks a greeting from the hour, one test at a time, and see how reordering the tests changes the answer.

learningObjectives: Trace an if/elif/else chain one test at a time to predict which block runs
Explain that Python runs only the first block whose test is True and skips the rest
Analyze how changing the order of elif tests can produce a wrong answer

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

keyQuestions: Why are the tests after the first true one never checked?
What greeting does hour 18 get, and why?
Which order of tests is correct, and how can you tell?
commonMisconceptions: Python checks every test and uses the last one that is true
elif tests run in any order
The else block runs whenever the first test is False
assessmentOpportunities: Students predict the greeting for any hour before stepping and are right at least 4 times out of 5.
Students explain why hour 12 gives "Afternoon" and not "Morning".
Students state a rule for ordering `<` tests: smallest limit first.

controls.label: Reset trace
controls.description: Returns the marker to the start

controls.label: Reorder tests
controls.description: Reverses the order of the three tests
